memory_candidates.content: When a task's implementation dispatch is interrupted mid-cycle, the next dispatch may inherit real uncommitted changes from the interrupted run (e.g. an index-entries.json line_count correction). Verify each such file's correctness against the actual current file state (e.g. `wc -l`) before including it in modified_files, rather than assuming it is either garbage or automatically correct.

For a 'live parity' verification phase where the plan's own acceptance bar asks to run a script's real (non-dry-run, side-effecting) path against production data, sandbox it: mirror the existing fixture suite's WORKDIR shape (synthetic .claude/scripts/ tree with real collaborator scripts copied in, --state-file pointed at a temp copy of the real state) so the check exercises genuine code paths (lock acquire, directory creation, mt_state_file writes) without mutating the actual repository.

When a full gate run (verify-deploy.sh, scripts/lint/*.sh) surfaces failures unrelated to the current task's file_scope, don't skip verification or silently ignore them: trace each via `git log --oneline -3 -- <file>` and a content diff of the check script itself to confirm the finding predates or is external to this task's commits, then close the phase [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with an evidenced Reasoned Exclusions table rather than either faking a fix or leaving the phase open indefinitely.
